verbatim: the four freedoms need to pretty much fundamentally inform, um, the the the core principles of this work.
subject: Osterweil's four freedoms as core principle
principle: Freedom to fail, to experiment, to fashion identities, and of effort are founding design principles.

verbatim: You can only use them a little bit if you only know them a little bit. When you master them, you can use their full power.
subject: Power scales with mastery
principle: Learned moves enter the player's deck; their strength grows with demonstrated mastery, giving intrinsic reason to master.

verbatim: You pick your intrinsic... your motivation system.
subject: Player picks the reward system
principle: Players choose their motivation mode (collector, meter, social progress) upstream, and it shapes the game they get.

verbatim: use visual rhetoric and design and iconography -- AS  A RULE start to use mnemonic icons.
subject: Mnemonic icons as a rule
principle: Teaching points carry mnemonic, compound iconography (pictogram-style) so symbols land as the point.
note: Human read: whether an icon lands is a Studio Eyes judgment.

verbatim: ALL of the images must advance a story. push something along.
subject: Every image advances the story
principle: No filler or repeated images; each frame pushes the story forward.

verbatim: each scene should have several easter eggs.
subject: Scenes hold easter eggs; replay varies
principle: Scenes tell story through objects of a lived life, and replay changes options and art slightly.

verbatim: Papercut is only one style.
subject: Art style is chosen per game
principle: Design specialists pick the art direction per game first; papercut is one option, not the house default.

verbatim: Super Sketchy tries not to HIDE that IT will be part of the studio that uses AI-assisted art.
subject: AI-assisted art is disclosed
principle: AI-assisted art is credited to Super Sketchy and never hidden.

verbatim: If showing part of the picture looks incoherent, advise before output.
subject: Halt partial output that reads as incoherent
principle: A partial build that looks incoherent is flagged to the founder before it ships.

verbatim: retitle the file that's been saved as archived so that I don't lose anything.
subject: Superseded builds are kept and marked archived
principle: When a later build replaces a file, the old one is retitled as archived, not overwritten.
note: Human read: the builds/ version folder is the current form of this.

verbatim: I want you to design a left throughout the companies that don't know they have a left.
subject: An Aleph for others
principle: The Aleph ('the left' in dictation) is a method the studio can offer other organizations, not only itself.

verbatim: at the very beginning of a design build, give back to me the founder the options of which agent... optimized agents and let me pick.
subject: Agent options at build start
principle: Each new build opens with recommended agent sets for the founder to choose from, given the design doc.

verbatim: offer novelty in each section of the hub so I can respond to discovered joy.
subject: Novelty in every hub section
principle: Hubs vary by section with surprises the founder can respond to, not uniform consistency.

verbatim: should be like sticky notes you can rotate and modify.
subject: Parking lot as editable sticky notes
principle: Parking-lot items are movable, editable notes that can be resolved or assigned; landing text fits on one screen.

verbatim: There should be different results. Different choices. That actually reveal parenting strategy.
subject: More than one win state
principle: Endings reflect the player's actual strategy; the title state is never the only win.
note: Raised on Dad Energy; applies to any game with an outcome screen. Human read.

verbatim: When you send me any asset employ at least 1 feature centering joy and novelty.
subject: Every delivered asset carries one joy feature
principle: No asset reaches the founder without at least one feature built for joy and novelty; the entry point matters most.

verbatim: Noonan task based high priority in games as core principle.
subject: Task-based design as core principle
principle: Games are built on task-based learning (dictated 'Noonan', likely Nunan); text matching alone is stale.

verbatim: when you add it, you have to have a note.
subject: Every played move carries a note
principle: Scaffolded moves come with a player's note when played: the plus-one value, not bare application.

verbatim: the moves that are available should be genre specific.
subject: Moves are genre-specific
principle: Workshop moves on offer change with the chosen genre.

verbatim: as a rule you need fact checking panelists not only in confluence but across all marketing and app output
subject: Fact-check all outward output
principle: Every marketing and app output passes a fact-checking seat, not only Confluence material.

verbatim: looks for cut offs hidden screen suboptimal buttons
subject: A seat checks every screen for cut-offs
principle: A reviewer optimizes output across screen sizes and catches clipped text, hidden controls and weak buttons.
note: Path check confirms a pre-ship gate exists; it covers contrast, not clipping. Clipping check still a wish.

verbatim: TSP uses compound metaphors as a way of reducing drift
subject: Compound metaphors reduce drift
principle: Naming systems through compound metaphor keeps the studio's work from drifting.

verbatim: compression. Lightness. Impact. Immediacy.
subject: Flash fiction principles for Workshop 4
principle: The flash fiction game teaches compression, lightness, impact and immediacy, mapped to EN195 outcomes.

verbatim: Use jenova chens flow stage movement system and credit him
subject: Credit borrowed mechanics
principle: When a game borrows a designer's system (Jenova Chen's flOw stages), the game credits him.

verbatim: including one that is totally just screen reader, you know, no motion mode.
subject: Comfort modes include screen-reader/no-motion and dark
principle: The one comfort button cycles modes that include a screen-reader, no-motion mode and dark mode.

verbatim: how do we tie this into the OS and not just make it be a wish list? We've had a real enforcement problem.
subject: Rules must be enforced, not wished
principle: A rule enters the OS only with an enforcement check; otherwise it is a wish.

verbatim: Log in how this game was made section in game and add system wide parallel.
subject: Each game shows how it was made
principle: Every game carries an in-game 'how this game was made' section (colophon or choice log), studio-wide.

verbatim: At the beginning and end of the game, make links to Tight Spiral Games land on and end page of app about the studio and the design process
subject: Games link to the studio at start and end
principle: A game's first and last screens link to a page about the studio and its design process.
note: Human read: no single link convention to check.

verbatim: you need to land in a scene and notice something no text that needs to be the starting point for all games
subject: Games open in a scene, not text
principle: Every game starts by landing the player in a scene where they notice something; no opening text.
note: Restates the standing 'scene first' rule. Human read per game.

verbatim: You have to improve visibility as a rule across all outputs
subject: Visibility is a rule on every output
principle: Text legibility is enforced on every output, not fixed case by case.

verbatim: The principle of my design is that the games are not gamification. They teach.
subject: Games teach; they are not gamification
principle: Learning principles drive the instructional design; points and badges layered on content are not the product.
note: Sits beside FV-183 ('Everything becomes a game'): play is everywhere, but games must teach. Human read.

verbatim: have the rhetorical situation drive the design all the time
subject: Rhetorical situation drives the art
principle: What the piece is trying to do decides the art style, every time.

verbatim: Start small. Make sure the right thing is good, small, and then magnify.
subject: Start small, then magnify
principle: Get the core small and right before scaling; founder filters the core content first.

verbatim: There's some cards that should be... there's only one of.
subject: Unique cards are marked differently
principle: Some writerly-move cards exist once (First Domino, After the Storm) and are marked apart from common ones.

verbatim: It's no dirty data. We announce what we're doing at all time. That's a founder principle.
subject: No dirty data
principle: Players are always told what is being gathered and why; opt-in is offered, and gates adapt rather than become floors.
note: Human read: needs a per-game data-disclosure convention to check.

verbatim: If it's no derivatives. We can't use it.
subject: No-derivatives licenses are out
principle: Open-licensed media is used only when the license permits adaptation; ND works are excluded.
note: Licensing is a legal seat's job, kept away from the founder. Human read.

verbatim: Consensus and calibration is how we build better systems.
subject: Consensus and calibration
principle: Systems are designed together through calibration and consensus voting, under founder principles.

verbatim: That is called recursive interviewing.
subject: Recursive interviewing
principle: The panel questions the founder based on his own ideas fed back to it, round after round.

verbatim: shields HALT data in builds that only me, founder, or TI HALT, etc, to release
subject: HALT items stay shielded until released
principle: Content can move forward while anything under a HALT stays shielded until the founder or the trauma-informed seat releases it.

verbatim: All TSP Products have Meta tags about what’s operative, current HITL tags
subject: Every product carries status meta tags
principle: Products are tagged with what is operative, where a human is needed, and where the founder is needed.
note: Human read: no tag convention fixed yet.

verbatim: It minimal at first but ringed down for depth for users wanted more info. That’s a choice point across system.
subject: Tiered depth on the meta layer
principle: The meta layer starts minimal and opens in rings for players who want depth (flOw-style levels).

verbatim: The intake form itself should be playful.
subject: A playful intake form
principle: Intake looks mostly normal until engagement, then plays: hungry empty boxes, lines that tilt, river lines showing relationships.

verbatim: We're not rewriting that work. We're giving them notes.
subject: Student work is never AI-rewritten
principle: Practice games give students notes on their own work; no AI-generated rewriting of what they wrote.
note: Human read; also a FERPA-adjacent boundary.

verbatim: make the contrast button have a left (less) right (more) and center (toggle skin)
subject: Contrast control: less, more, toggle skin
principle: The contrast control has less on the left, more on the right and a center skin toggle.
note: Same shape as FV-010 (- O +). Human read.

verbatim: I like being shown options side by side as graphics.
subject: Options shown side by side as pictures
principle: Design choices reach the founder as side-by-side visuals, not lists.

verbatim: Anyone can have dad energy. Not just guys.
subject: No gendered assumptions in game copy
principle: Copy does not assume the player's gender; an identity seat reviews alongside the trauma-informed one.
note: Raised on Dad Energy. Human read.

verbatim: ALL TIGHT spiral games must land in a scene, simple, intuitive, impactful.
subject: Land in a scene or get closed
principle: Every game opens on a simple, intuitive, impactful scene; files that underwhelm on open get closed.
note: Restates FV-212 in its strongest form. Human read.

verbatim: add dignity first framing as a core concept for OS, decide weight.
subject: Dignity-first framing in the OS
principle: Dignity-first framing is a core OS concept; its weight is still to be decided.

verbatim: Recursive engagement has to be a core of this studio.
subject: Recursive engagement, not dopamine
principle: Engagement comes from joy and positive motivation, studied recursively, not from attention-capture loops; it shapes the business model too.

verbatim: a key principle of this has to be microlearning and then stacking stacking moves.
subject: Microlearning with visible move-stacking
principle: Players learn small moves and stack them, and the stacking is made visible (the glass engine).

verbatim: by only text validation, no AI generation, always look... using, uh, validated sources
subject: Real people's words come from verified sources
principle: Quotes and actions of real public figures come only from transcripts, verified press or records, never generated.
note: Raised on Choose Your Leader. Human read: needs a citation convention to check.

verbatim: Put the game design system in the playable game, and don't make me go back and forth between screens.
subject: Feedback instruments live inside the game
principle: Playtest and design feedback tools sit in the playable build, not on separate screens.

verbatim: you can build an asset, and then you can park it, and somebody interacts with that
subject: Single player plus asynchronous multiplayer
principle: Games support solo play and asynchronous multiplayer: one player builds and parks an asset, another interacts with it later.

verbatim: You can't copy the system.
subject: Know the gears; don't copy the runbook
principle: The recursive principle is notice, experiment, adapt, with attention to joy; copied pipelines miss the gears.

verbatim: it has to be adaptive and collapsible or else people are gonna go crazy with the options.
subject: Intake is adaptive and collapsible
principle: Intake asks what the work teaches and how it is assessed, but stays adaptive and collapsible so options never overwhelm.

verbatim: we need a TIGHT SPIRAL basic palette for default until game specs tell different.
subject: A studio default palette
principle: A Tight Spiral default palette applies until a game's spec says otherwise.
note: Possible tension: on 2026-07-14 the founder said 'Forget about default palette' while asking which helpful defaults had proved hurtful. Raised for the founder.

verbatim: Let them design skin themselves.
subject: Players design their own skins
principle: Players can design skins, including options no current interface offers, grounded in design science.

verbatim: it has to have metaphor, amplification, or even exponential using three metaphors.
subject: Titles compound metaphors
principle: Game titles carry metaphor and amplification, ideally three metaphors compounding.

verbatim: the stated and measured value principes of the core design (TI, choice, play, joy)
subject: Core design values: TI, choice, play, joy
principle: Trauma-informed design, choice, play and joy are the stated and measured values the advisory board is trained in.

verbatim: Every game should have a wireframe novelty.
subject: Novelty from the wireframe
principle: Each game's novelty is designed in at wireframe stage, not added at the end.

verbatim: Too much on a page. Start with the image. A tap flips the image “card” to the story.
subject: Image first; tap to flip to story
principle: Screens lead with the image; a tap flips it to the story, and questions sit below.
note: Raised on Dad Energy, ordered applied across the build. Human read.
